agency_full: European Space Agency (Mercury Planetary Orbiter + Mercury Transfer Module) / Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (Mercury Magnetospheric Orbiter, Mio)
payload: 4100 kg launch stack: MTM (Mercury Transfer Module, ESA — 4 ion thrusters, solar arrays) + MPO (Mercury Planetary Orbiter, ESA, 1230 kg, 11 instruments) + MIO (Mercury Magnetospheric Orbiter, JAXA, 285 kg, 5 instruments) + MOSIF sunshield. Two science orbiters separate after Mercury arrival.
credit: © ESA / JAXA / Airbus. BepiColombo launched 2018-10-20 from Kourou — the joint Europe-Japan flagship to Mercury, named after Giuseppe (Bepi) Colombo, the Italian mathematician who designed Mariner 10's multi-flyby trajectory. The 7-year cruise uses 9 gravity assists (Earth 2020-04-10, Venus 2020-10-15, Venus 2021-08-10, then six Mercury flybys 2021–2024) plus continuous ion-electric thrust from the Mercury Transfer Module to bleed off the enormous solar-gravity gradient between Earth and Mercury orbits. Mercury orbit insertion is set for 2026-12-05, with science operations beginning early 2027 after MTM jettison and MPO + Mio separation. Primary science: Mercury's exospheric composition + dynamics, the composition of its iron-rich crust and Caloris-class large impact basins, the structure of its magnetic field + magnetospheric tail, and tests of Einstein's general relativity via radio-science range tracking through Mercury's strong solar-gravity environment. Nominal one-year mission with one-year extension authorised.
